newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-KASHIMA SURVIVE PENALTY SHOOTOUT TO STAY TOP OF J LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KASHIMA SURVIVE PENALTY SHOOTOUT TO STAY TOP OF J LEAGUE.

text.p: Kashima Antlers squeezed out another win on penalties on Saturday to stay on top of the J.League table while Yokohama Flugels remained at their heels with a last-minute victory.
The Antlers beat Urawa Red Diamonds 5-4 on penalties after a goalless draw in extra time on a slippery, rain-soaked pitch at Tokyo's National Stadium.
Kashima, who beat Jubilo Iwata on penalties last Wednesday, and Yokohama are on 63 points, three clear of Nagoya Grampus Eight, with Kashima still ahead on goal difference.
Urawa dropped a notch to sixth place with 56 points and fell out of contention for the championship with only two more matches to go.
Flugels midfielder Sampaio headed home the winning goal in the dying minutes to stage a 2-1 victory over title holders Yokohama Marinos at Mitsuzawa stadium.
Nagoya stole a 4-2 triumph on penalties at home against JEF United Ichihara following a 1-1 draw which saw Nagoya's Go Oiwa score his first J.League goal with a 37th-minute equaliser.
Jubilo Iwata remain in fourth place with 59 points after overwhelming Cerezo Osaka with a 3-0 home victory as Italian forward Salvatore Schillaci notched up his 14th goal of the season.
Kashiwa Reysol striker Edilson struck twice in the second half to help his team to a 3-0 home win against Sanfrecce Hiroshima. Edilson and Evair of Yokohama Flugels lead the league with 20 goals.
Lowly visitors Kyoto Purple Sanga beat Bellmare Hiratsuka 1-0 for their fourth straight win and Shimizu S-Pulse gained a 3-1 away victory over Avispa Fukuoka.
